text:
anya: Quick follow-up on the resident-score smoothing idea from the RFC — I ran a couple of sims overnight and have questions.

kai: cool, summary please? :eyes:

anya: TL;DR: EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.15) reduces noisy thrashing when lots of tiny batches hit different embeddings, but it increases warmup lag; prefetching using smoothed scores needs throttles.

michael: nice. What workload did you run? bursty chat or embed-heavy? any perf numbers?

anya: ran two profiles: 1) chatbot mix (50% short chat, 30% medium, 20% long-gen) 2) embeddings-heavy (many small 768-d vectors). For chat mix: median p95 latency unchanged, p99 improved ~4% because fewer eviction-induced stalls. For embeddings: token throughput dropped ~6% with same eviction budget.

tara: interesting. So smoothing helps latency SLOs for gen workloads but hurts throughput for high-cardinality embeddings.

anya: exactly. The problem: smoothed resident_score retains staleness — items that were hot briefly remain "hot" in the residency window and block prefetch slots for truly hot newcomers.

kai: can we make smoothing adaptive? like alpha = f(request_rate) or decay faster on high churn?

anya: I tried a hybrid: EWMA with adaptive alpha where alpha = clamp(0.05, 1/(1+rate_norm), 0.5). It helps: embeddings throughput loss cut in half, gen p99 still good.

michael: can you share the config snippet you used? saves a ton of guessing.

anya: sure:

```yaml
resident_score:
  method: ewma
  base_alpha: 0.15
  adaptive:
    enabled: true
    rate_norm_window_ms: 2000
    min_alpha: 0.05
    max_alpha: 0.5
prefetch:
  max_slots: 12
  per_tenant_limit: 4
  fairness: true
```

tara: how did prefetch max_slots interact with smoothed scores? any regressions from prefetch starving normal eviction paths?

anya: with max_slots=12 and per_tenant_limit=4, prefetch queue occasionally starved eviction when alpha low (very smooth). So I added a backpressure hook: if eviction_pending_counter > 8 then prefetch_throttle=true.

kai: that sounds like a good short-term fix. Long-term: we should consider separating "recency" vs "frequency" signals instead of cramming both into one score.

michael: agree. frequency should be slow-moving (EWMA) while recency should be spike-detect and decay quickly. Then prefetch uses recency, eviction prioritizes frequency.

anya: sketched an API for that — two scores per page: freq_score and recency_burst. Then resident_score = w1*freq + w2*recency for legacy compatibility. Prefetch uses recency_burst > threshold.

tara: that'd help explain telemetry too. We can have separate histograms for freq and recency and alert on divergence.

michael: any rough perf model? cost delta vs p99 latency improvements?

anya: rough numbers from sim: separating signals yields net win: embeddings throughput impact gone, gen p99 improved ~6% vs baseline. Memory churn down 12%.

kai: awesome. What about implementation complexity? double book-keeping, extra counters per page.

anya: it's a small add: one extra counter (recent_hits) with a fast decay tick (~100ms) and freq_ewma. We already sample hits.

michael: watch out for extra contention on hot counters at scale. Use sharded counters or per-core deltas.

anya: yes using per-core delta + periodic fold-in in the sim.

tara: next steps? RFC follow-up or spike PR?

anya: propose: 1) land adaptive alpha flag behind feature flag (2 weeks) 2) perf tests in staging for both workloads (3) open RFC for dual-score model with telemetry plan.

kai: +1. please include the prefetch backpressure hook in the short-term rollout.

perf-bot: perf-run: resident-score-adaptive-alpha — 12h run complete. Results uploaded: https://internal.redwood/perf/9791234567

michael: thanks, can you paste the p99 numbers in the RFC draft so reviewers don't need to chase the perf dashboard?

anya: will do. I'll draft a short RFC with the dual-score proposal and include config examples, perf tables, and a rollout plan. Planning to sync next Tue.

tara: sounds good. @kai can you help review the telemetry portion?

kai: yep, happy to.

anya: thanks all :thumbsup:
